results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if repository is unknown/ambiguous)] [Prerequisite]: Identify candidate repositories using GITHUB_FIND_REPOSITORIES (select one repo to scope later calls).

[Optional (if default ref/branch targeting is uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Validate repo metadata using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (capture default ref); use GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES when you must read/search a non-default ref.
[Required] [Step]: Run repository-scoped queries using GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE (use repo qualifier; try multiple simple keyword/symbol/path variants) and collect matched file paths.
[Optional (if results seem capped/incomplete)] [Next Step]: Expand coverage using GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE_ALL_PAGES (dedupe matches by file path before opening files).
[Optional (if search returns zero matches or path/casing is uncertain)] [Next Step]: Enumerate likely paths using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE (verify non-truncated), then choose candidate files to open.

[Required] [Next Step]: Retrieve selected files (or list a directory when unsure / after a 404) using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (handle file-vs-directory shapes; decode only when encoding indicates base64).

[Fallback (if inline content is missing/truncated, preview-only, or file is large)] [Fallback]: Retrieve content using GITHUB_GET_RAW_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (handle locator-style or temporary-link responses and retry if expired).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE] Results are capped (around 1000) and may be incomplete; HTTP 403 can occur under search/rate limiting.
[GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE] Overly complex queries can fail with HTTP 422; split into multiple simpler searches.
[GITHUB_GET_A_TREE] Large recursive trees may be truncated; treat truncated output as incomplete coverage.
[GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] File vs directory responses differ (object vs array); base64 content may include newlines that must be stripped before decoding.
[GITHUB_GET_RAW_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] May return a locator/temporary download link rather than inline bytes; links can expire and require rerunning the tool.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Robust base64 extraction/decoding for GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT wrapper variations
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import base64

def dig(d,ks):
  for k in ks:
    if not isinstance(d,dict) or k not in d: return None
    d=d[k]
  return d

obj=result if isinstance(result,dict) else {}
b64=dig(obj,['data','data','content']) or dig(obj,['data','content']) or dig(obj,['response','data','data','content']) or dig(obj,['response','data','content']) or ''
raw=base64.b64decode(b64.replace('\n','')) if b64 else b''
raw.decode('utf-8',errors='replace')[:2000]
```

GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE.description: Searches code file contents and paths on the default branch of GitHub repositories using a query string; searches only files under 384KB, returns max 1000 results by best match, and is optimized for precision.

q.description: Code search query, including keywords and qualifiers (e.g., `language:python`, `user:octocat`, `repo:owner/repo`). For full syntax and qualifiers, see GitHub docs: [Constructing a search query](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#constructing-a-search-query) and [code search qualifiers](https://docs.github.com/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-code).

page.description: Page number for results. For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

sort.description: DEPRECATED. Valid: 'indexed' (sorts by last indexed time) or 'updated' (sorts by last updated time). If unspecified, results sorted by best match. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

order.description: DEPRECATED. Order ('asc' or 'desc') for results; effective only if `sort` is specified. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

per_page.description: Results per page (max 100). For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.description: Retrieves a file's Base64 encoded content or lists a directory's contents from a GitHub repository.

ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.

path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.

repo.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: Required. The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive. Can also accept full repository path in format 'owner/repo' - the repo part will be extracted automatically.

GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE_ALL_PAGES.description: Tool to search code across multiple pages using GitHub's code search API. Use when single-page searches may miss matches and you need a full or capped result set. GitHub caps results at ~1,000 total items regardless of pagination; results for broad queries may be silently truncated. Only the default branch is indexed, and very large files may be excluded — treat results as potentially partial. Rate limit: ~30 requests/minute; honor `Retry-After` on 403/429 responses.

q.description: The search query string for code search. **IMPORTANT**: While GitHub's documentation mentions boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) support, the REST API still uses older syntax that frequently rejects queries with operators or parentheses (ERROR_TYPE_QUERY_PARSING_FATAL). For reliable searches, avoid boolean operators and parentheses. Supports qualifiers: `language:`, `repo:`, `path:`, `extension:`, `user:`, `org:`, `in:file`. Multiple terms use implicit AND: `hello world` finds both. Quote exact phrases: `"exact phrase"`. For complex boolean logic, use multiple separate API calls or the GitHub web interface.

sort.description: Sort field: only 'indexed' is valid (sort by last indexed time).

limit.description: Optional cap on total number of items to retrieve across pages (min 1).

order.description: Sort order for results: 'asc' or 'desc'. Only effective when `sort` is provided.

accept.description: Custom Accept header for media type (e.g., `application/vnd.github.text-match+json` to include text match metadata).

per_page.description: Number of results per page (min 1, max 100).
